notes.title: Version 0.67.1
notes.notes:
The big equipment update exits beta this week, but we'd like to focus on our reasoning behind the enemy changes. You can view the full list of changes here.

Area 1, Shakuzen Square, was notoriously tough on higher difficulty levels. Many high Ascension runs ended at Akane, the boss of the area. While we don't mind the occasional early game loss, the extreme difficulty of Area 1 meant that you often didn't get to make many choices before your run was over. We still want your decisions to matter, and Area 1 will still be noticeably harder on high Ascension, but the changes should make it much less likely for bad luck to end your run before it can even start. We also made several of Area 1's enemies less defensive in general, as this could cause some fights to stall out when using more defensive character artifacts.

The other areas haven't received any sweeping changes, but we took a look at the stats, and enemies which were underperforming or overperforming have been adjusted accordingly. Aria and Maribel weren't outliers in terms of power, but they were often very annoying due to how many Status cards were put directly into the player's draw pile. This often led to dead turns whenever you drew 4-5 Status cards at once. We wanted to reduce how frequently this occurred, while still keeping the Status cards relevant. Those encounters now use cards that apply Statuses to hand or discard instead. This means the damage will still rack up, without denying as many draws.

Let us know what you think of the changes! If you want to give us your feedback directly, consider joining our Discord. If you want to experience future content a week in advance, you can join the beta branch using the game's Steam settings. The patch notes are posted every Sunday.

notes.title: Version 0.66.1
notes.notes:
Today, Stella Ingram will be added to the hard pool of Silent Forest, completing the enemy pool for that area. Her signature card is Break of Dawn, which causes the first card played each turn to cost 0 for both sides.

Last time, we added Lilith, with the goal of discouraging the high cost cards that you often default to in the late game. Stella is the opposite. She appears in the early to mid game, when your deck is likely to have cheap, low rarity cards. By adding her to Silent Forest, and giving her fight a strong incentive to run high cost cards, the player is encouraged to pick up equipment that they might otherwise ignore.

We like the incentives that Stella creates for deckbuilding, though we are aware that the heavy cost reduction from Break of Dawn can create large amounts of burst damage that lead to very swingy gameplay. We're keeping an eye on her for now, though there are no changes to her decklist at this time. Let us know what you think of the new encounter.

notes.title: Version 0.65.3
notes.notes:
Today, Lilith Ambrose will be added to Hall of Judgment with no changes from the beta branch, making it the first area to have the full suite of seven enemies.

We've been quite happy with the way that Lilith has played. Hypnotic Gaze is the most important card in the matchup, discouraging high cost cards, excessive card draw, and cards with Focus. Hall of Judgment is designed to encourage you to change your equipment to deal with threats as they appear, and Lilith incentivizes a deck not needed for any other fight in the game.

In a way, Lilith acts as the counterpart to Arriet Harper. Arriet encourages you to have more impactful cards, while making cheap and spammable cards much less useful. Lilith does the opposite, encouraging you to empty your hand each turn to minimize the damage taken from Hypnotic Gaze. Hypnotic Gaze also has synergy with Charm, Evil Eye, and Captivate, which makes her deck feel more cohesive. It also plays well with the many Curse effects she uses. We hope you will enjoy fighting Lilith as much as we did.

notes.title: Version 0.64.6
notes.notes:
Nerissa Hart is leaving beta today, joining the cast of Silent Forest. Every area now features six different enemies, though we plan to bring that total to seven by the end of Early Access.

Though Torozu does have Waterfall, Nerissa is the first enemy to use a deck reliant on the Flow mechanic. Ceaseless Flow ensures that Flow is relevant every turn, and she has powerful attacking options like Scald and Tsunami that strongly encourage the player to disrupt Flow whenever possible. It isn't as simple as attacking every turn, though, because Lifesaver and Whirlpool are capable of producing enormous amounts of Block. The fight is intended to incentivize a healthy mix of offense and defense. Silent Forest can be somewhat stall-heavy, so we like the gameplay that Nerissa encourages.

notes.title: Version 0.64.1
notes.notes:
Ethel Vance, the first addition to Terminal Station, is leaving beta this week.

Though Terminal Station is the ranged area of the game, we generally include a few enemies capable of fighting at the opposite range to prevent trivializing the entire area with range locking effects. Aurelia fulfills this role in the easy pool, and Ethel does the same for the hard pool.

She can be seen as a counterpart to Victoria. Both fights are fairly difficult to beat just by attacking. Victoria is mostly a scaling check, since Deflector Shield effectively gives her much more health than normal. Ethel is a defense check, to see if you can consistently protect yourself until she dies to Core Meltdown. Currently, there aren't many fights that check your ability to block consistently, with Kira being the only other one. Ethel is intended to make purely defensive cards more viable during her battle.

notes.title: Version 0.63.2
notes.notes:
Arriet Harper, the first addition to Hall of Judgment's encounter pool, is moving out of beta this week.

As the final area of the game, Hall of Judgment is designed to ask different things of the player with each battle. Arriet is the first opponent to use time magic, and her signature card is Time Stop. She's designed to counter decks that play a large number of cards each turn. She's also the first ranged opponent in Hall of Judgment, which had a rather strong melee lean up until now.

We don't have much data on Arriet yet, since not all runs survive until Hall of Judgment. While most enemies that were moved out of beta have received no changes, we anticipate that Arriet's deck may need to be adjusted in the future, as Hall of Judgment enemies are the most difficult to fine-tune.

notes.title: Version 0.62.1
notes.notes:
With Kira Seine moving out of beta, we wanted to briefly talk about her history and design. Crown is a game about constantly changing your build. To encourage that, each enemy is designed to be a unique threat that incentivizes certain types of deckbuilding.

Amaya Everill was formerly responsible for the entirety of the block manipulation theme. However, this didn't really encourage you to build your deck in a specific way. Cards like Assassinate would punish you for blocking, while Shuriken Barrage would punish you for not blocking. We decided to split this theme into two separate characters. Amaya still uses the various piercing attacks, while Kira now has cards with additional effects when fully unblocked. This means that a deck that's effective against Amaya is unlikely to perform well against Kira.

Based on testing of last week's beta patch, Kira is effectively fulfilling her new role in Restless Parish. As a result, we are implementing her directly with no changes to her deck.

notes.title: Version 0.61.2
notes.notes:
This week’s patch serves primarily as preparation for next week's larger update. That update will feature a brand new enemy and about 250 new pieces of equipment.

Currently, each area is split into two easy encounters, two hard encounters, and a boss. But there's only two possible easy fights, and two possible hard fights. This means that, up until this point, you've been guaranteed to encounter every enemy at some point throughout the run.

Our plan is to get each area up to three easy encounters and three hard encounters, so while you'll still have to prepare for the possibility of any given enemy, runs will have some threat diversity.

With that out of the way, here's a bit of a teaser for the enemy who will be joining the hard pool in Restless Parish:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45162839/96be2ebd375444bcfab7dc92a5b6ce3d333b96e3.png

To keep everyone's interest, we're adding a couple of the new cards in advance and adding them to existing equipment and upgrade pools. As usual, the update is exclusive to the beta branch for now, but we plan to move it over to the main branch when the next patch is released. 

If you haven't already, please join our Discord! It's a small community, so you'll have a lot of input during Early Access. Stay tuned for next week!
